records.found: Two registry entries for ongoing trials were updated in the window: the maker's phase 3 of MACI against bone marrow stimulation in ankle defects (updated 2026-11-05), and a phase 3 of CARTISTEM (donor cord-blood stem cells, not the person's own cells) against debridement in knee cartilage damage and osteoarthritis (updated 2026-11-05). Neither is a trial result, and neither is own-cell treatment of worn older knees; small papers on grown-cell repair in middle-aged (50 to 65) patients appeared but do not meet the wide-use test.

findings.what: Registry update to MACI phase 3 in ankle (talus) defects, ages 17 to 65, 309 planned, started 2026-05-28, primary completion 2030-07. Ankle, not knee osteoarthritis.

Registry update to CARTISTEM phase 3 versus debridement for knee cartilage lesions and osteoarthritis, ages 18 to 75, 300 planned, started 2026-03-11. The cells are donor umbilical-cord-blood stem cells, so it does not match 'a person's own cells', but it is the first phase 3 of a cell product in knee osteoarthritis the record's registry check did not list.

Cartilage journal: 12 patients aged 50 to 65, grown-cell implant with knee osteotomy, better repair scores at second-look arthroscopy than osteotomy alone; patient-reported outcomes did not differ between groups. Small, non-randomised.

records.found: In its third-quarter results of 2026-11-02, Vertex said it is now focusing on its newer islet-cell therapy VX-017, which suits more patients than zimislecel (made only for blood types A or A/B), and expects to start pivotal development of VX-017 in 2027. The release reports no filing for approval of zimislecel and does not repeat the earlier plan to give updated zimislecel timelines.

findings.what: Vertex third-quarter 2026 results (exhibit 99.1 to its 8-K): focus moves to VX-017, pivotal development expected 2027, Fast Track granted; zimislecel limited to blood types A or A/B; zimislecel's only mentions are in this comparison. No filing for zimislecel is reported.
